cards.definition: Courses hold quizzes, quizzes hold cards
cards.explanation: Make a course for each class, like Biology, and a quiz for each chapter. The sidebar lists them all.
Type its name right away, or rename it later on its page. Two courses can not have the same name.

cards.definition: New quiz, on a course page
cards.explanation: It opens in Edit quiz, where you name it and add cards.

cards.definition: The sidebar and the top row
cards.explanation: The button beside Shrimply Study hides or shows the sidebar. The top row shows where you are: click a part of it to go back. Every page has its own address you can bookmark.
Saves everything as one .shrimp file. A * in the tab title means changes you have not downloaded yet. This browser keeps a copy between visits, but the file is your real copy.
It replaces what is in the app, and asks first if you have changes you have not downloaded. Open your file on another device, a phone too, to study there. Your cards are never uploaded anywhere.

cards.definition: Danger zone, at the bottom of the page
cards.explanation: For a course, on its page. For a quiz, in Edit quiz. It asks first and can not be undone.

cards.definition: Theme, at the bottom of the sidebar
cards.explanation: Pick one of five dark themes. This browser remembers it; it is not saved in your file.
Edit quiz is on the quiz page. Fill in the term and the definition. Enter goes to the next field, then to a new card; Shift+Enter starts a new line. The trash icon deletes a card.
Paste one card per line, with a tab or " - " between term and definition. A Quizlet export or spreadsheet rows work. Check the preview, pick where the cards go, then add them.

cards.definition: Add fill in the blank, in Edit quiz
cards.explanation: Type a sentence, select a word, then Mark as blank (Ctrl+B). Each blank is asked as its own question. Blanks can sit inside each other.

cards.definition: The Explanation button on a card
cards.explanation: Optional background, shown after you answer under More info. A fill-in-the-blank card has one per blank.

cards.definition: The image button beside a field
cards.explanation: Or paste or drop an image on the field. The term, the definition and a fill-in-the-blank card can each have one. Click the thumbnail to replace it, its ✕ to remove it. A side still needs its text.
Where a click already does something, like on a flashcard, rest the pointer on the image until its border closes. Esc or any click closes it.
A named, colored part of a quiz. Multiple choice takes wrong answers from the same group first, so they are harder to tell apart. Click its dot for another color, its arrow to fold it shut.

cards.term: Put a card in a group
cards.definition: The group menu on the card
cards.explanation: Import can also add cards straight to a group. Ungroup removes a group but keeps its cards.
Back to the quiz page. Empty cards and groups are removed. A half-filled card turns red and keeps you here until you fix it.
First pick the mode, the side you see and the order. Your picks stay for the next round.
Click the card or press Space to flip it. Then pick Didn't know (1) or Knew it (2).
Press 1 to 4 to pick. A quiz needs at least 2 cards for it.
Case, accents, punctuation and extra spaces don't count. For a typo or another right wording, "I was right"counts it as right.
Term shows the term and asks for the definition, Definition does the opposite, Mixed picks one for each card. A fill-in-the-blank card always asks its blanks.
It shows the right answer, and which card a wrong answer belongs to. If the card has an explanation, the round button above the sheet opens More info. Continue (Enter) goes on.
Space flips a flashcard. 1 and 2 rate it, 1 to 4 pick a choice. Enter checks and goes on. The arrow keys scroll long text. Esc leaves the round.
Works while studying, in the results and on the quiz page. The change shows right away.

cards.definition: Retry missed, on the results screen
cards.explanation: You see your score and every question, with filters for Missed, Right and Marked (where you used I was right). Study again asks every card again.

cards.definition: Only a term and a definition

cards.explanation:
The explanation is optional plain text.
Line breaks are kept, like this one.
"termImage": "1.svg" shows images/1.svg on the term side.

cards.term: A shape with four equal sides
cards.explanation: "definitionImage": "2.svg" shows images/2.svg on the definition side.
This card names 1.svg too: cards can share an image file.

cards.statement: A fill-in-the-blank card marks each {blank} with braces.
cards.explanation: One blank, so the explanation is plain text.

explanation: With several blanks, the explanation is a list with one entry per blank.
Blank 3, inside blank 2. Blanks are counted in the order of their {.

cards.statement: Write \{ and \} for braces that are not blanks, and \\ for a {backslash}.
cards.explanation: A backslash before a brace makes it a plain brace, not a blank. Two backslashes make one plain backslash. JSON doubles every backslash, so in library.json they look twice as long as in the app.
A fill-in-the-blank card can have one image: "image": "1.svg".

cards.definition: A named part of a quiz
cards.explanation: Its cards go in the group's own "cards" list, not the quiz's.

cards.definition: lagoon, coral, sky, sand, moss, rose, clay, slate

cards.explanation: Here that is lagoon, since sky is taken.
library.json at the top of the zip, plus an images folder when cards have images. Zip the files themselves, not a folder around them.
version is always 1. Nothing else goes at the top.
Both are required. The name can not be empty or only spaces, or the same as another course's (case, spaces and punctuation do not count). "quizzes" can be an empty list.

The name can not be empty or only spaces, or the same as another quiz's in its course (case, spaces and punctuation do not count). "cards" holds the cards that are not in a group and can be an empty list.
color is one of lagoon, coral, sky, sand, moss, rose, clay, slate. The name can not be empty or only spaces, and up to 50 characters fit the editor.
A card with an empty term or definition is skipped while studying.
type is always "cloze". A statement needs at least one blank to be studied.

Each blank is one question, and its text is the answer. Blanks can sit inside each other. A blank can not be empty, and the same text can not be marked twice. A backslash before a brace makes it a plain brace.

cards.definition: Text for one blank, a list for several
cards.explanation: The list has exactly one entry per blank, in the order of their {. Use "" for a blank without one.

cards.definition: A file name from the images folder
cards.explanation: png, jpg, jpeg, gif, webp, avif or svg. "1.svg" means images/1.svg, and that file must be in the zip.
No HTML or Markdown. Line breaks are kept. Spaces and empty lines at the start and end are dropped.
A field that is not listed in these rules stops the file from opening. The error names the spot, like courses[0].quizzes[1].cards[3].
Keep answers short enough to type and put background in the explanation. Use groups for the parts of a topic, so multiple choice offers close wrong answers. Multiple choice needs at least 2 cards.

Download this guide, rename it to .zip and unzip it. Replace Your course with your own cards, by hand or with an AI, following these rules. Zip it again, rename it to .shrimp and open it. If it does not open, the error names the spot.
